responseMessageContents.text:
Thank you—this is useful evidence.

It proves the AWS account-recovery case was opened in **your name (Ivan Perez)** and that you are working to regain root MFA access. But it also confirms AWS will not discuss or change the account until you sign in as the root user, so I cannot safely remove or rotate any AWS access yet.

**Safe next step:**
1. Complete AWS’s root-MFA recovery steps.
2. Once signed in, create an IAM admin user owned by you, enable MFA, and save backup recovery methods.
3. Send a screenshot of the IAM Users page showing your new admin user and `Rork1`—hide account ID and access keys.
4. I will then switch the app to your owner IAM credentials, verify it works, and disable only the old `Rork1` credentials.

Your code, GitHub repo, Render service, and production app remain unchanged.
